subject: Islamic Religious Studies
examFormat: The aim of the UTME syllabus in Islamic Studies is to prepare candidates for the Board’s examination and to test their achievement of the course objectives: to master the Qur’an and Sunnah as foundations of Islamic and social life; to be familiar with Islamic heritage, culture and civilization; to be acquainted with the tradition of Islamic scholarship and intellectual discourse; to demonstrate knowledge of Islamic moral, spiritual, economic, political and social values; to be exposed to the fundamental principles of Islam; and to be prepared to face the challenges of life as good practising Muslims. The syllabus has three parts: the Qur’an and Hadith; Tawhid and Fiqh; and Islamic History and Civilization. It states no exam format.
